summary: A decentralized identifier gives a person, an agent or a thing a name that its own controller holds, rather than one an account provider issues. The core specification is a finished web recommendation from July 2022 and it covers three things well: the shape of the identifier, the document it resolves to, and which key may be used for which purpose. It deliberately stops short of everything after that. It carries no claims about a person, no protocol for handing credentials over, and it states that what happens once an identifier holder has proved control is left to each method and each application. Two traps for a working group: the newer revision is not finished, having sat at candidate stage since March 2026 past the earliest date it could have advanced; and no concrete method is standardized at all, with 269 of them listed, as of 7 September 2026, in a group note that says in its own words that listing is not endorsement.

coverage.note: Specifies the identifier syntax, the document data model, the core properties and the abstract resolution process for a name its subject controls; what is missing is any standardized method for creating such a name, and the revision that would supersede version 1.0 has not advanced past candidate stage.
